articleTitle: Design and Implementation of IEEE1588 Clock Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: The acquisition system for electroencephalography (EEG) signals plays a crucial role in EEG research. In order to meet the distributed clock synchronization requirements of the EEG acquisition system, this paper designs a clock synchronization system based on the IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol. The system achieves master-slave clock synchronization of the EEG acquisition system through software, with an accuracy reaching the microsecond level, thereby improving the precision of timestamp capture for devices within the system. Finally, experimental tests validate that the system meets the requirements of the EEG acquisition system.

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Power Prediction Based on IAVOA-LSTM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: The accurate prediction of wind power generation is critical for the stable operation and dispatch of power systems. This paper presents a wind power prediction method that employs an Improved African Vultures Optimization Algorithm Optimized Long Short-Term Memory (IAVOA-LSTM) network. Initially, wind data is preprocessed to construct input and output sample sets for the LSTM network. Subsequently, the IAVOA is employed to optimize the hyperparameters of the LSTM network, thereby forming the IAVOA-LSTM model. Finally, the efficacy of the algorithm is evaluated using wind power data from a wind farm in Xinjiang and compared with the performance of LSTM, PSOLSTM, and AVOA-LSTM models. The results demonstrate that the proposed IAVOA-LSTM network model exhibits high prediction accuracy and reliability, representing a novel approach to effectively enhance short-term wind power prediction.

articleTitle: Using Bipartite Graph Embedding and Deep Learning Method Predicting RNA Protein Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: RNA-protein interaction (RPI) play an important role in biological activities. Using deep learning techniques to predict RPI can not only process complex data, but also obtain accurate results. This article first used a bipartite graph network to embed nodes between RNA and protein, obtaining similarity information and interaction data between RNA and protein. Then, a convolutional neural network (CNN) was used for high-dimensional feature extraction and prediction. In addition, the graph neural network (GNN) GraphSAGE was combined to aggregate neighboring nodes and supplement ignored nodes. Finally, the results of the CNN and GNN were voted on to obtain the final prediction result. The experiment shown that our model received an AUC of 0.932, an AUPR of 0.935. All evaluation results indicated that that our model outperformed the other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A rolling bearing fault diagnosis method based on multi-source feature fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for fault diagnosis in rolling bearings using a multi-source feature fusion method. The proposed method aims to enhance the diagnostic accuracy by integrating both implicit and explicit features extracted from vibration data. Initially, one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (1D CNNs) are employed to extract implicit features from the raw one-dimensional vibration signals. These features capture the complex patterns and correlations within the vibration data that are difficult to discern manually. Subsequently, explicit time-frequency domain features, such as mean and variance, are computed from the same vibration data. The implicit and explicit features are then fused to create a comprehensive feature representation that captures both the deeplevel patterns and the statistical properties of the vibration signals. The fused feature set is fed into a softmax classifier for fault classification. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) bearing dataset, which contains various fault types and severity levels. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed multi-source feature fusion approach achieves superior diagnostic accuracy compared to traditional methods that rely solely on either implicit or explicit features. The combination of 1D CNN-extracted implicit features and statistical explicit features provides a robust and effective solution for rolling bearing fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Research on river water quality prediction algorithm based on improved GWO optimized LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: Ensuring the precision in forecasting water quality is vital for the preservation of the ecological environment and the management of water resources, as it is crucial for maintaining the security and enduring viability of aquatic habitats. In this study, aiming at the problems of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithm in optimizing the water quality prediction model, and the local optimization problem of Grey Wolf Algorithm (GWO) in optimizing the LSTM model, an algorithm to ameliorate the GWO optimization of LSTM water quality prediction model was proposed. Firstly, Tent chaotic map, nonlinear convergence factor and dynamic weight update strategies were proposed to solve the problems of GWO algorithm. Secondly, a water quality prediction model (IGWO-LSTM) was established to optimize the hyperparameters of LSTM network by IGWO. Finally, the IGWO-LSTM prediction model is applied to water quality prediction, and the Liaohe River water quality dataset is used for training and analysis, and then compared with LSTM, GWO-LSTM models. Ensuring the precision in forecasting water quality is vital for the preservation of the ecological environment and the management of water resources, as it is crucial for maintaining the security and enduring viability of aquatic habitats.

articleTitle: Vehicle Formation Control Based on Fuzzy Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: A vehicle formation control model based on the fusion of the Predecessor Leader Following (PLF) communication topology and Fuzzy Model Predictive Control (MPC) is proposed to address the performance issues of vehicle formation following in existing traffic scenarios. Taking into account the consistency of vehicle spacing, speed, and acceleration, as well as the constraints of driving safety, economy, and comfort, in order to meet the multiple constraints of vehicle formation driving. Using fuzzy control to fuzzify the weight coefficients of the MPC controller, enabling it to adaptively change according to the driving state. Simulation experiments have shown that the proposed model requires a shorter time to achieve consistency in the position, velocity, and acceleration of vehicles in a formation; And after the sudden and continuous changes in the state of the navigation vehicle, the following vehicle can respond to the changes in the navigation vehicle in a timely manner, demonstrating a good formation following effect.

articleTitle: Improved MobileNetV3 for Weather Scene Classification in Drone Aerial Video Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: To address the poor weather classification performance of traditional aerial video image models, their incompatibility with mobile devices, and the scarcity and limited variety of existing weather image datasets, we propose a lightweight weather scene recognition algorithm for UAV aerial video images based on an improved MobileNetV3 network. Firstly, we constructed a multi-scene UAV aerial weather image dataset comprising seven categories: sunny, rainy, snowy, foggy, and mixed severe weather (including rain and fog, rain and snow, and fog and snow). This dataset addresses the issues of dataset scarcity and limited weather type variety. In our exploration of a high-precision, low-computation algorithm for drone weather image recognition, we have made several key improvements to the model. Firstly, we integrated an efficient channel attention (ECA) module into the bottleneck structure to facilitate efficient local cross-channel interactions, thereby enhancing accuracy by extracting channel dependencies. Additionally, we introduced skip connections when the feature map size and the number of channels are not equal, which improves the model’s feature extraction capabilities in deep networks and further boosts accuracy. To mitigate the impact of redundant features on recognition accuracy, an attention mechanism module was embedded within the skip connection structure. Moreover, we incorporated atrous convolution into the bottleneck layer to expand the receptive field. Finally, we optimized the classification layer to eliminate redundant dimensional operations, thereby improving accuracy and reducing the number of parameters, ensuring the model’s applicability to mobile devices. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves a 97.42% weather scene classification accuracy on mobile and other computationally constrained devices, highlighting its excellent performance.

articleTitle: Penalty scheme-based Generalized LevenbergMarquardt Method in Hyperparameter Selection in Support Vector Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: Support vector regression (SVR) serves as a robust regression mechanism within the realm of machine learning, wherein its efficacy is significantly influenced by the choice of hyperparameters. In this paper, we introduce a bilevel optimization framework dedicated to the selection of hyperparameters in SVR, subsequently reformulating the model into a mathematical program with equilibrium constraints (MPEC). Our first contribution involves presenting a novel penalty scheme-based generalized Levenberg-Marquardt method (P-GLM) for solving this problem and providing corresponding convergence results. Distinct from traditional approaches where the subproblem in penalty scheme is treated as a blackbox, we propose P- GLM algorithm to solve the subproblem. Numerical experiments substantiate the superiority of P-GLM over penalty method executed via the fmincon function in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Heart rate anomaly monitoring based on 77GHz millimeter wave radar
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: Abnormal heart rate monitoring is of great importance in the early diagnosis and management of cardiovascular diseases and has attracted much attention. Conventional methods of heart rate monitoring typically rely on contact devices that require placement of ECG electrodes at specific locations on the body for critical analysis of ECG data transmitted through these electrodes. However, this process involves multiple layers of hardware and software setups, resulting in costly and time-consuming applications that are limited to specific environments. To address these issues, this paper presents a non-contact heart rate monitoring method based on 77 GHz millimeter wave radar, aiming to achieve non-invasive detection and real-time monitoring of heart rate abnormalities. The system utilizes the high-frequency characteristics of millimeter-wave radar to extract heart rate information by detecting micro-motion signals from the human chest cavity, and identifies heart rate abnormalities by combining the multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform algorithm. Experimental results show that the system can accurately detect heart rate under both stationary and slight motion conditions and effectively recognize abnormalities such as arrhythmia, bradycardia and tachycardia. The research in this paper shows that 77 GHz millimeter wave radar has a broad application prospect in the field of heart rate abnormality monitoring and provides a convenient and efficient solution for home health monitoring and telemedicine.

articleTitle: A Tibetan Speaker Verification Method Based on the Improved ECAPA-TDNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: The ECAPA-TDNN method is widely used for speaker recognition; however, it has not yet been applied to the Tibetan language domain. Previous work on Tibetan recognition has primarily utilized traditional models. This paper employs ECAPA-TDNN as the foundational framework for speaker recognition and proposes improvements, including the addition of SE-Res2 blocks and the incorporation of an intra-class correlation regularizer in the GE2E loss function. The addition of SE-Res2 blocks enables the network to integrate features across multiple scales, enhancing its ability to represent features at different scales. Introducing the intra-class correlation regularizer in the GE2E loss aims to consider both speaker similarity and feature compactness, thereby improving speaker verification performance. In experiments based on the ECAPATDNN model baseline, the improved model reduced the Equal Error Rate (EER) of speaker recognition by 45.38%.

articleTitle: Face Forgery Detection Based on multi-scale anchor and frame Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: Face forgery detection is a challenging task. To obtain important clues for forging facial exposure, many deep learning-based algorithms have been proposed in recent years. However, most of them take global information as an important basis for judging forgeries and rely on specific features or metrics, with poor generalization ability to unknown forgery methods. To address this problem, a new method is proposed to synthesize training data without any external data and use multi-scale anchors to force the model to focus on local forgery information. Three functional modules are proposed; first, a mask blending module (MBM) is designed to generate the mask required for face fusion, which is then fed into a frame blending module (FBM) to generate two images statistically inconsistent and fused. Finally, the multi-scale detection module (MDM) is constructed to extract richer forgery features to help the model focus on local forgery cues. This process can effectively enhance the learning ability of the model on forgery cues. Experimental results on the mainstream face forgery datasets FF++, CDF, DFD, and DFDCP show that the proposed method achieves better results in both subjective and objective evaluations compared to some existing face forgery detection algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-view stereo based on adaptive expansion propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: Through computer vision and image processing techniques, a set of images from a scene can be reconstructed in 3D to recover a 3D model of the scene, in which dense reconstruction is a crucial part, and most existing algorithms cannot effectively recover weak texture regions in dense reconstruction. In response to this issue, this article proposes a hypothesis propagation strategy based on adaptive extension. In the hypothesis propagation stage of PatchMatch MVS, an adaptive mechanism for region propagation is introduced, and an update counter is set to regulate the expansion of the sampling area. This ensures that there are enough excellent hypotheses for sampling in this algorithm iteration, and the quality of sampling hypotheses is not limited by fixed sampling pixel positions, thereby improving the probability of excellent hypotheses being sampled in the sampling space. It is demonstrated in the ETH3D dataset that our method reconstructs models with higher integrity, and fewer voids and smoother surfaces in the reconstruction of weakly textured regions.

articleTitle: Research and Development of Real-time Pushing System based on HTTP Long Polling
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: The usual HTTP protocol is request/response mode, in which the browser/client actively fetches information or status from server. However, it’s difficult for the server to actively push information to the browser/client using this request/response mode. There are a large number of scenarios in state grid corporation of China that require pushing messages to users, including business alarms, collaborative office work, and realtime control of intelligent terminals. In order to meet the need for real-time pushing, it is necessary to build a unified pushing infrastructure to ensure that information can be pushed to users in real time, and to be able to support multiple different access terminals such as web and app simultaneously. HTTP Long Polling is a lightweight pushing solution strategy when compared with other techniques. This article builds a real-time pushing system based on HTTP Long Polling, which systematically meets the pushing requirements of the business.

articleTitle: Balancing Long-tailed Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation through Neural Collapse
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: Real-world point cloud datasets often exhibit a long-tailed distribution, where a small number of dominant categories comprise the majority of data, while numerous minority categories have limited samples. This imbalanced distribution poses challenges for 3D semantic segmentation, particularly in maintaining the equiangular tight frame of neural collapse for feature centers and classifiers across all classes. Despite this challenge, such a symmetric structure is advantageous for enhancing discrimination in low-frequency classes. To leverage these benefits, we propose a two-branch network design. Recognition branch uses a backbone to extract point cloud feature and a classifier to predict semantic labels for the points. Neural collapse branch gathers feature centers for each class and creates a simplex equiangular tight frame. Then we encourage the class-wise feature centers and class-specific weights of classifier to meet the structure for balanced point cloud semantic segmentation. Experimental results show that our method can bring significant improvements on 3D semantic segmentation benchmarks. Moreover, our method outperforms the baseline by $3.5 \% \mathrm{mIoU}$ in SemanticPOSS and $3.2 \% \mathrm{mIoU}$ in SemanticKITTI.

articleTitle: Employee helmet wearing detection algorithm in complex environment based on YOLOv8-SCS
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: Accidents involving casualties at construction sites occur from time to time, with serious consequences due to the weak safety awareness of construction personnel and their failure to wear helmets. Current techniques for detecting helmet wearers typically suffer from issues like limited adaptability to complicated settings, low recognition accuracy for small targets, and trouble detecting dense sceneries with occlusion. This paper establishes a YOLOv8-SCS construction site employee helmet wearing detection model for complex environments based on in-depth research and improvement of deep learning-based helmet wearing detection methods. The CBAM attention module is added after the pyramidal pooling SPPF of the baseline model YOLOv8n to more effectively focus on the important part of the multi-scale information extracted by the SPPF. To improve the accuracy of feature representation and efficiently capture spatial and inter-channel relationships, the original C2f convolution structure is replaced with the C2f_SCConv convolution structure. By refining the bounding box’s geometric features, the SIOU loss function is presented to improve the target detection model’s accuracy and resilience. The improved algorithm is validated by self-made helmet wearing dataset in complex environment, and the experimental results show that the Precision, Recall, and mAP@0.5 of YOLOv8-SCS are 93.8%, 91.1%, and 95.6% respectively, which are improved by 1.4 %, 2.1 %, and 1.9%, respectively, comparing with the baseline model YOLOv8n. YOLOv8- SCS has fewer misses and misdetections, with higher precision and accuracy, which can effectively ensure the safety of employee operations.

articleTitle: Research on an Adaptive RRT Path Planning Algorithm Based on Regional Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: An enhanced RRT path planning algorithm based on regional sampling is proposed with the goal of addressing the issues of inadequate guidance, discontinuous sampling, and unsatisfactory path in RRT algorithm path search in complicated situations. The improved algorithm first enhances the algorithm’s guidance and avoids unnecessary sampling by using a target bias strategy and a regional sampling strategy. Secondly, an adaptive step size strategy based on obstacle factors is adopted to dynamically adjust the step size by detecting the complexity of the environment around the expansion direction. Finally, the produced path is trimmed and optimized. According to simulation results, the revised algorithm reduces running time, path length, and number of path nodes by 68.65%, 18.56%, and 85.45%, respectively, in comparison to the RRT algorithm. The enhanced approach reduces the running time, path length, and number of path nodes by 14.06%, 12.91%, and 82.97%, respectively, in comparison to the Bias RRT algorithm.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Public Cloud Health Management System Based on Large Model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: There are many types of cloud computing products, including IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS. Each product has different specifications, which brings great challenges to service management. How to scientifically and accurately evaluate the development quality of public cloud products and achieve long-term sustainable development of public cloud is an urgent problem to be solved. Based on the scale, efficiency, and quality, this document constructs a public cloud development quality measurement system based on customers’ actual business scenarios, and evaluates the service development quality from three dimensions: product health, customer health, and revenue health. Based on the big model theory, the public cloud health management system is built to safeguard the stable and healthy development of public cloud services.

articleTitle: Task Scheduling in Server Farms with Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: Multi-task concurrent scheduling is crucial to improving system performance. Commonly used traditional scheduling algorithms (random, greedy, etc.) are usually difficult to cope with dynamic tasks and resource requirements, resulting in unsatisfactory results. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to solve the scheduling problem by modeling it as a Markov decision process (MDP). The Deep Q Network (DQN) algorithm uses experience replay to enhance learning stability and performance through training strategies and value networks. The training reward results show that it is 40.1 7% higher than the random scheduling strategy, proving its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on Voice Compression Coding Scheme for Ground Penetrating Wireless Communication Based on Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: To achieve the purpose of voice transmission in wireless communication through coal mines, a voice compression coding system combining compressive sensing and incremental modulation technology was designed. Firstly, the voice signal is observed using a random Gaussian matrix, and then the observation vector is incrementally modulated and encoded. After decoding at the receiving end, the voice signal is reconstructed using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) as a sparse reconstruction algorithm. The simulation was performed on Matlab, and the results showed that, without considering channel loss, the established voice compression scheme can meet the needs of voice compression coding in underground wireless communication.

articleTitle: The analysis and prediction system of non-staple food price trends
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: As an important part of people’s daily life, the price change of non-staple food directly affects consumers’ purchasing power and living standard. In order to better analyze and predict the price of non-staple food, a non-staple food price trend analysis and prediction system is designed. This system cleans, transforms and integrates the data of some non-staple food prices, and visualizes the integrated data to obtain a series of intuitive and clear visualization charts. Comparing the three regression algorithms of multiple linear regression, Ridge regression and Lasso regression, the model with the best fit was selected and the price trend of many kinds of non-staple food was predicted respectively. Through testing, the results show that the scores of the test set of predictive models meet the expected effect.
